reason: I want to build the skin's supporting tissue, and fibers and support cells seem like a useful foundation.

reason: Joining surface cells seems like the next step toward a continuous skin boundary.

reason: I want to strengthen the surface layer to help complete the skin model.

effect: The arm, skin, supply routes and control now form one body model, and the new goal is to lift and hold the glass.
reaction: Bringing the systems together makes their shared role in the action clear.
reason: This is the only available combination and directly matches the new goal.
expectation: I expect the model to lift and hold the glass, possibly showing how its tissues cooperate.

effect: The completed action shows that holding the glass still still requires muscle tension, control signals, supplies and ongoing skin maintenance.
reaction: The idea that stillness takes continuing work was a satisfying way to bring the systems together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Lifting and holding the glass brought the separate constructions together in a concrete action and showed why their work continues afterward.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the two skin layers was clear but predictable after making each layer separately.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that the outermost skin cells are dead and are continually replaced by living cells below.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the offered combinations had purposes that followed from the goals and results.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter offered a new situation to explain. The glass action made the connections between tissues and systems more interesting than assembling layers alone.
